linkedin.about:
I’m the host at Netflix’s new show, "How to Get Rich," and the New York Times best-selling author of “I Will Teach You To Be Rich.” I’m also the Founder and CEO of IWT, where we host over 1 million readers/month on business, careers, negotiation, psychology, and money.

My family is from India and my parents immigrated to the States in the 1970’s. With four kids and one income, they couldn’t afford to send me to college so I built a system to apply to 60+ scholarships. I worked hard to earn a full ride to Stanford.

But when I got my first scholarship check, I invested it in the stock market…and immediately lost half my money. Oops.

That’s when I decided to learn how money really worked. I quickly realized most money advice was irrelevant for people like you and me:

❌ Most money advice is about restriction. 
❌ Money is too confusing. Where are you supposed to start? And who do you trust?
❌ Nobody was talking about money psychology.

Fast forward to today. What I believe now:

✅ I believe in asking $30,000 questions, not $3 questions. Buy all the lattes you want.
✅ There’s a limit to how much you can cut, but no limit to how much you can earn.
✅ Your Rich Life is yours. I consider it a tragedy to live a smaller life than you have to.

HOW CAN I WILL TEACH YOU TO BE RICH HELP YOU?

At IWT, we now have a worldwide community of people who want to create their Rich Lives, their way. Here you’ll find:

➡️ The best free advice on money. Everything from earning more to how to live your Rich Life.
➡️ Earnable, our signature digital program that has helped over 30,000 people to start a business.
➡️ Money Coaching Program, which has a vibrant community who want to get skilled at their finances.

Start living the life you’ve always wanted to. 

GET THE CONSCIOUS SPENDING PLAN:
📥 iwt.com/csp-linkedin

positions.description:
After receiving my first scholarship in high school, I invested it in the stock market and immediately lost 50%. That's when I decided to learn something about personal finance. Since then...

http://www.iwillteachyoutoberich.com hosts over 1,000,000 readers/month, where I help people automate their finances so they can get on with their lives.

I've been featured in media like the Today Show, New York Times, Wall Street Journal -- all because we *know* we need to learn personal finance, but none of us actually do it. In 2009, I published "I Will Teach You To Be Rich," which became an instant Amazon #1 best-seller and a New York Times bestseller.

I combine my experience in social influence and persuasion with personal finance to focus on the tactical and psychological aspects of behavioral change. 

Money is first. 

Next up...?

education.description:
We launched PBwiki (now called PBworks) in 2005, making it easy to create a powerful wiki for online collaboration.

I ran marketing and usability for PBwiki, which involves a focus on the user experience and viral marketing. I also handled strategic partnerships and managing support for a user base of millions of users.

Omidyar Network is a "mission-based investment group committed to fostering individual self-empowerment on a global scale" (it's Pierre Omidyar's organization to effect social change).

Previously, I consulted on social psychology here. Later, I sourced and evaluated investment opportunities.

Captology (Computers as Persuasive Technologies) involves the combination of technology and persuasion. 

I've been a researcher and director in the Lab, where I've created experimental methodologies, analyzed data, and communicated our findings to others.

More recently, I spoke about persuasive technology in places like Japan and around the Bay area.

Read more: http://captology.stanford.edu

Storm brought me on to help get everyone up to speed on how young people are using technology. What's this Web 2.0 thing? Why are social networks important (and are they really just a fad?). Are college kids afraid of being sued for downloading music? How do mobile phones fit into the picture?

I made presentations and brought in experts to share the viewpoints of my generation.

Now here's the corporate version: Focused on emerging Internet technologies & investment evaluation. Worked closely with entire firm to source and evaluate deals.

I worked first as an intern, then was hired to stay on as a consultant to the CEO.

My initial job was to devise a viral-marketing strategy for AuctionDrop. After that, I studied and recommended changes for the end-to-end customer experience.

I was Seth's first-ever intern. I managed this by cold-calling him and convincing him that I could do it.

Since then, Seth has realized the value of interns and continues to hire them even today.

We worked on the book Free Prize Inside, which became a New York Times bestseller (and a WSJ bestseller, too).

I met/interviewed Fortune 500 CEOs and other innovators across industries and organizations. 

I was also a member of the strategy team for political-marketing site, which used classic persuasion and viral-marketing elements.

Coursework included theoretical and applied persuasion, entrepreneurship, computer science, human-computer interaction research and design, psychology, and policy analysis of the impact of emerging technologies on society.

I wrote a comedy column and ran projects in social entrepreneurship, captology, personal finance, and religious studies.
I studied social influence and persuasion in a study-abroad tutorial, and ate horrible, horrible food. My papers are online at http://www.RamitSethi.com.

posts.caption:
You’re good at your job. Your friends are great. You like your life.

So why does dating feel like the one thing you can’t figure out?

Most people blame the apps, their schedule, or the idea that there just aren’t any good people left. But a lot of the time, the real problem is closer to home: how your week is set up, the habits that take over when dating feels uncertain, and whether your standards are protecting you or just keeping you from trying.

Next Wednesday, October 14 at 12pm ET / 9am PT, dating coach and matchmaker Blaine Anderson is joining Rich Life Expert Sessions to walk you through the four places people get stuck, and the one change you can make this week.

Comment DATING and I’ll send you the link to register for free.

Still moving money between accounts every payday? You can set that up once and let it happen automatically.

My free Money Made Easy download shows you, step by step, how to split your paycheck between investments, savings, and bills—so everything goes where it needs to go automatically.

Comment START and I’ll DM you the link.

Already automated your money? What’s been the biggest relief?

These are my Money Rules.

If you had to create 3 Money Rules for yourself, what would they be? I love hearing your Money Rules!

By the way, I notice a funny thing: when people create their first rules, they’re almost always restrictive:

Don’t spend on ____
Never buy ____
Go for the generic ____

I’ll ask, “Does that rule excite you?”
They laugh. “Not really”

PICK EXCITING RULES!

Use my free Design Your Rich Life mini course so you can say YES to more. Comment “DESIGN” and I’ll send you a DM with the link.

A lot of you have asked me to set up I Will Teach You To Be Rich for single people who want to meet each other.

Here’s the next best thing.

On Wednesday at 12pm ET / 9am PT, dating coach and matchmaker Blaine Anderson (@datingbyblaine) is joining our next Expert Session. She’s helped thousands of people figure out what’s really getting in the way of their dating life, and she’s going to show you the reasons yours might not be working, plus the simple, practical changes you can make this week.

If you’re single, don’t miss this one. Comment DATING and I’ll send you the free link to register.

You can only cut so much.

Skip the lattes, cancel every subscription, cook every meal at home. At best, you free up a few hundred dollars a month. Then you hit the floor.

But there’s no ceiling on the other side.

Making an extra $500 a month on the side is the same as getting a $6,000 raise. An extra $1,000 a month is a $12,000 raise.

Most people never try because they think they need a brilliant idea, a lot of money, or to quit their job. You don’t. You need one idea people will pay for, and you’re probably already good at something that could become one.

Comment CHALLENGE and I’ll send you my free 3-day challenge to find yours. You’ll also save your seat for my live session on Monday, Oct 19.

Here’s why you should pause before you make any of these moves:

Rushing to pay off a house
→ Now what? You have ongoing costs and sacrificed decades of investment gains so you could own a house “free and clear.”

Cashing out investments to pay debt
→ It feels so great to be debt-free! Except you lost decades of investment gains.

Partner quitting because childcare costs are high
→ Could be a very valid decision, but before you make this highly consequential move, did you carefully decide—together—which expenses you’ll cut? How about the ones that may grow? What about re-entry into the workforce? What if the primary earner loses their job?

When I talk about $3 questions vs. $30,000 questions, this is what I mean. Coffee won’t make a material change in your finances, but these decisions will.

And notice what most of them have in common: they get made under pressure. The mortgage feels heavy, the debt feels urgent, childcare eats a paycheck. 

Extra income changes that. It gives you options. 

It’s the difference between making these decisions because you HAVE to and making them because you WANT to.

Comment CHALLENGE and I’ll send you my free 3-day challenge to find a business idea you could start on the side. You’ll also save a free spot for my live session on Monday, Oct 19.

You can make $185,000 a year and still end up fighting over the prices at Target.

When there’s no plan, every purchase becomes a debate. Dinner out, a concert, a quick store run. But when you know your numbers, you don’t have to argue about each one. You already know the answer, yes or no. And sometimes the answer will be no. That’s part of having a plan.

Comment CSP and I’ll send you my free Conscious Spending Plan template to help you and your partner decide in advance what you’ll spend on, so you can stop fighting over every purchase.

▶️ Watch and listen to “Money For Couples” on Spotify, YouTube, or wherever you get your podcasts.

This commenter noticed something that happens on the podcast all the time.

When I even question private school, it’s an immediate no. Sometimes there are tears, even for couples who are drowning in debt.

I get it. No parent wants to feel like they’re shortchanging their kids.

But that reaction isn’t about the numbers. It’s an invisible script: “Good parents pay for private school.” And when something is off-limits before you’ve even looked at it, it’s not a decision anymore. It’s a rule someone else wrote for you.

Private school can be a great choice. It’s also one of the biggest Fixed Costs a family can take on, and it deserves the same scrutiny as everything else.

Comment MONEY MINDSET and I’ll send you my free Money Mindset Mini Course, so you can spot the invisible scripts behind your biggest money decisions.

I love meeting people in our community. When I ask what the most important parts of their Rich Life are, 99% of the time the answers are health, relationships, and career.

But when I follow up with, “What have you spent money on lately to invest in these things?”

Silence.

I always say, “Show me someone’s calendar and their spending, and I’ll show you their priorities.”

The fix is to get specific. “I want time and freedom” gives you nothing to work toward. “I want to spend a month in NYC every year” tells you exactly what to plan and save for.

Comment JOURNAL and I’ll send you the first chapter of the IWT Journal. It walks you through designing your Rich Life, down to what each goal costs and when you’ll make it happen.

If you keep asking where the money for a trip is going to come from, the answer is usually that there was never a plan.

Avoiding that reality doesn’t make the money appear. It just pushes the disappointment down the road. The fix isn’t another vague conversation. It’s deciding ahead of time how much goes toward the things you care about, like travel.

Comment CSP and I’ll send you my free Conscious Spending Plan template so you can plan for the trips you want instead of hoping the money shows up.

▶️ Watch and listen to “Money For Couples” on Spotify, YouTube, or wherever you get your podcasts.

They’re in their early 30s. They’re maxing out their retirement accounts. And they’re investing even more on top of that.

Now they want to know: “Are we saving too much for retirement?”

I ran their numbers and told them exactly what I’d do.

Comment NEWSLETTER and I’ll send you the link to get my full breakdown in Saturday’s email.

Supporting your partner’s dream shouldn’t mean ignoring the numbers.

When you’re $633,000 to $1 million in debt with no retirement, this isn’t about long-term wealth anymore. It’s about protecting your family. And sometimes the most loving thing you can do is ask the hard question: When is it time to call it?

Comment MONEY TALK and I’ll send you my free guide on how to talk to your partner about money, including the conversations you’ve been putting off.

▶️ Watch and listen to “Money For Couples” on Spotify, YouTube, or wherever you get your podcasts.
